subject: Literature
title: Phillis Wheatley: The Enslaved Poet Who Amazed the World
description: Learn Phillis Wheatley: The Enslaved Poet Who Amazed the World in one minute.

hook.text: Phillis Wheatley was kidnapped from Africa, enslaved in Boston, and became the first African American to publish a book.

buildup.text: Her 1773 book of poems astonished readers who could not believe an enslaved Black woman could write sophisticated verse.

discovery.text: She had to defend her authorship before a panel of eighteen white men who examined her to prove she actually wrote her poems.

twist.text: Thomas Jefferson dismissed her work, revealing that even Enlightenment thinkers could not overcome their racial prejudice.

climax.text: Wheatley's mere existence as a published poet challenged the entire intellectual justification for slavery in America.

punchline.text: She wrote her way into a history that tried to erase her.

quiz.question: Why did Wheatley have to appear before a panel of eighteen men?
options: To receive a literary prize for her poetry
To prove she had actually written her own poems
To request permission to publish from colonial authorities
